title: Hedge Fund Manager - India Roadmap
description: The ultimate roadmap to becoming a Hedge Fund Manager in India, navigating SEBI's AIF regulations, building a verifiable track record through feeder roles like proprietary trading or equity research, and understanding the '2 and 20' compensation model.

nodes.label: Hedge Fund Manager and their Responsibilities
nodes.description:
A Hedge Fund Manager is an elite investment professional who manages a pooled investment fund that can use a wide variety of complex strategies to generate high returns for its investors. Unlike traditional mutual funds, hedge funds are less regulated and can take both long and short positions, use leverage (borrowed money), and invest in derivatives.

In India, hedge funds operate under the regulatory framework of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) as Category III Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs). These funds are open only to sophisticated investors like Ultra High Net Worth Individuals (UHNIs), family offices, and institutions who understand the high-risk, high-return nature of the strategies.

A Hedge Fund Manager's role is multi-faceted:

  • Chief Investment Officer (CIO): They are the ultimate decision-maker, responsible for defining the fund’s investment philosophy and strategy (e.g., Long/Short Equity, Global Macro, Event-Driven).
  • Portfolio Manager: They actively manage the fund's portfolio, making buy/sell decisions, managing position sizes, and executing trades.
  • Risk Manager: They are obsessed with managing risk. This involves setting risk limits, hedging unwanted exposures, and stress-testing the portfolio against adverse market scenarios.
  • Entrepreneur & Fundraiser: In most cases, the manager is also the founder of the fund. This requires them to raise capital from investors, manage investor relations, and run the business side of the fund.

This is not an entry-level job; it is the culmination of a highly successful career in investment management or trading.

stages.title: The Prerequisite Path: Building Your Track Record

nodes.label: Elite Education & Foundational Experience
nodes.description:
The path to becoming a hedge fund manager is not linear but is always built on a foundation of exceptional academic credentials and, most importantly, a proven, verifiable track record of generating returns (alpha).

  1. Education: An impeccable academic record from a top-tier institution is a filtering mechanism. The most common backgrounds are:
    • IITs/Top Engineering Colleges: For managers who will run quantitative or algorithmic funds.
    • IIMs (A,B,C)/ISB: For managers focused on fundamental, research-driven strategies.
    • CA / CFA Charterholders: A very common background for long/short equity managers due to the deep financial analysis skills.
  2. Crucial Work Experience (The Feeder Roles): You cannot become a hedge fund manager without 10-15 years of exceptional performance in one of these roles:
    • Proprietary Trader: This is a direct path. If you have a successful multi-year P&L track record trading a firm's capital, you have the core skill required.
    • Buy-Side Equity Research Analyst / Fund Manager: Managing a portfolio at a mutual fund or PMS and consistently outperforming the benchmark is another classic path.
    • Sell-Side Equity Research Analyst: A star sell-side analyst who has made a series of highly profitable and accurate stock calls ('alpha calls') over many years can also make the leap.

The key is building a portable, auditable track record. Investors will not give you capital without it.

nodes.label: Setting up a Category III AIF in India
nodes.description:
Once a track record is established, the next phase is entrepreneurial.

  • Regulatory Registration: This involves registering the fund with SEBI as a Category III AIF, a complex legal and compliance process.
  • Building the Infrastructure: This means selecting and partnering with key service providers: a custodian to hold the securities, a fund administrator for NAV calculation, and auditors.
  • Capital Raising: The most challenging part. It involves creating a pitchbook, marketing the strategy, and convincing the first set of anchor investors (LPs or Limited Partners) to invest capital. The initial capital is often raised from personal networks.
  • Compliance & Operations: Ensuring the fund adheres to all SEBI regulations, including reporting, risk management, and disclosure norms.

nodes.label: Roles and Career Opportunities
nodes.description:
The primary role is managing the hedge fund itself, but hedge funds offer multiple high-impact roles.

  • Founder / CIO: Defines strategy, manages capital, and oversees risk.
  • Portfolio Manager (PM): Runs specific strategies or books within the fund.
  • Research Analyst: Performs deep fundamental or quantitative research to generate investment ideas.
  • Quantitative Analyst: Builds models, trading systems, and statistical strategies.
  • Trader: Executes trades efficiently and manages execution risk.
  • Risk Manager: Monitors exposure, drawdowns, and tail risks.

The Indian hedge fund ecosystem includes multiple Category III AIFs and alternative investment platforms operating across equity, macro, and quantitative strategies.

nodes.label: Compensation Structure – The '2 and 20' Model
nodes.description:
Compensation in hedge funds is highly performance-driven and follows the global '2 and 20' fee model.

  • Management Fee ("2"): 1.5%–2% of Assets Under Management (AUM) charged annually. This covers operating costs such as salaries, systems, compliance, and infrastructure.
  • Performance Fee ("20"): 15%–20% of profits generated, typically above a minimum return threshold known as the hurdle rate.

Example: A fund managing ₹500 Crores generates a 25% annual return (₹125 Crores profit). A 20% performance fee results in ₹25 Crores earned by the fund manager.

  • Analysts / Junior PMs: Base compensation ranges from ₹40–80 LPA+, with bonuses linked directly to fund performance.
  • Founder / CIO: No upper limit. Earnings scale directly with AUM and performance and can reach tens or hundreds of crores for top-performing funds.

This is a high-pressure, high-risk career. Sustained underperformance can result in capital withdrawals and fund shutdown.
